subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity source, thresholds, nudge delivery, kill behavior, and user-visible notification contract should own it?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested capability, but implementing it changes core runtime recovery, config defaults, parent wake behavior, and channel-visible status, so automation should not choose the policy unilaterally.

options.title: Define a core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt a maintainer-owned design that specifies deterministic activity tracking, compatibility-safe defaults, staged nudge delivery, terminal escalation, and bounded parent/channel notification before implementation.

options.title: Prototype default-off recovery
options.body: Allow a narrower opt-in experiment with explicit config and tests while leaving existing long-running subagent behavior unchanged by default.

options.title: Defer to timeout and manual controls
options.body: Keep automatic activity-based kill out of core and route remaining recovery to explicit runTimeoutSeconds, status APIs, and manual kill/reap controls.

recommendation.title: Define a core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a maintainer-owned design that specifies deterministic activity tracking, compatibility-safe defaults, staged nudge delivery, terminal escalation, and bounded parent/channel notification before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across subagent registry, timeout, reconciliation, and runtime recovery surfaces.
